device.name: RWARE tiny warehouse with one agent

facts.text: The normal registration loop registers rware-{size}-{agents}ag{diff}-v2 with entry_point rware.warehouse:Warehouse for the tiny, small, medium and large layouts, the default, easy and hard difficulties and 1 to 19 agents; for tiny, 1 agent and the default difficulty the id is rware-tiny-1ag-v2

The registered tiny layout uses column_height 8, shelf_rows 1, shelf_columns 3, n_agents 1, msg_bits 0, sensor_range 1, request_queue_size 1, max_inactivity_steps None, max_steps 500 and individual rewards
The Action enum has five actions: NOOP=0, FORWARD=1, LEFT=2, RIGHT=3 and TOGGLE_LOAD=4
The action space is a Tuple with one Discrete(len(Action)) per agent, which is a Tuple of one Discrete(5) for the registered one-agent layout
The Direction enum has four values: UP=0, DOWN=1, LEFT=2 and RIGHT=3
The default observation space is built by _use_fast_obs: it flattens each per-agent sub-space of the slow observation space into a Box and returns a Tuple with one Box per agent
The sensor window of an agent has (1 + 2 * sensor_range) ** 2 cells, which is a 3x3 window at the registered sensor_range 1
The grid height is (column_height + 1) * shelf_rows + 2 and its width is (2 + 1) * shelf_columns + 1; the goals are the two cells in the middle of the last row
A reset recreates the shelves, spawns the agents at random grid locations with random directions and samples the request queue from the shelves using np_random
step maps each tuple element to an Action and a forward move of an agent carrying a shelf into a standing shelf is cancelled to NOOP
A requested shelf delivered to a goal is replaced in the request queue by a uniformly sampled shelf that is not currently requested
With RewardType.INDIVIDUAL the agent that delivers a requested shelf to a goal receives +1
The episode reports done when max_inactivity_steps or max_steps is reached; truncated is always False
The environment metadata declares the render modes human and rgb_array at 10 frames per second

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the agent positions, directions and request queue, and the transitions are deterministic; this package's fake draws from Python's random.Random while upstream draws from numpy's np_random, so one seed does not give the same trajectory on the two implementations

gaps: the environment is a discrete grid-world kinematic model: positions, headings, shelf pick-up and delivery and episode counters are modelled directly; there are no continuous dynamics, forces, contacts, actuators or sensors

no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and the environment has no physical timestep, so timestep_ms is 0 and one tick advances one discrete transition (warehouse.py:933-946); a receipt reports tick, not simulated milliseconds

the Gymnasium bridge carries one scalar reward while upstream Warehouse.step returns one reward per agent (warehouse.py:946); the registered layout has one agent, so the fake returns that single reward as a float

the fake backend re-implements the one-agent tiny layout in pure Python and was not compared with a run of the upstream environment; it seeds Python's random.Random instead of numpy's np_random and has no multi-agent collision graph, rendering or gymnasium wrapper chain
snapshot and restore are not offered: Warehouse exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
